title: Flat base change of the conormal algebra of a closed immersion
statement:
Let $g:X\to X'$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $i':Z'\hookrightarrow X'$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I'$, and let $(Z,i,f)$ be the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] of $g$ and $i'$, so that $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ is a closed immersion with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I$ and $f:Z\to Z'$ satisfies $g\circ i=i'\circ f$. Let $\mathcal G'=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal G'_n$ and $\mathcal G=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal G_n$ be the conormal algebras of $i'$ and $i$ [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra], and let $f^*\mathcal G'$ be the pulled-back quasi-coherent graded $\mathcal O_Z$-algebra [def-pc-module-pullback]. There is a unique morphism of graded $\mathcal O_Z$-algebras
$$c:f^*\mathcal G'\longrightarrow\mathcal G$$
such that for every pair of affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$, $U'=\operatorname{Spec}R'\subseteq X'$ with $g(U)\subseteq U'$, writing $I'=\mathcal I'(U')$ and $I=\mathcal I(U)=I'R$, the map $c$ on sections over $i^{-1}U$ is, under the identifications of [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra], the map
$$\bigoplus_{n\geq0}(I'^n/I'^{n+1})\otimes_{R'}R\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n/I^{n+1},\qquad [a]\otimes r\longmapsto[g^\sharp(a)\,r].$$
In degree $0$ it is the identity of $\mathcal O_Z=f^*\mathcal O_{Z'}$, and in degree $1$ it is the canonical conormal map $f^*\mathcal C_{Z'/X'}\to\mathcal C_{Z/X}$. The map $c$ is surjective. If $g$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], then $c$ is an isomorphism of graded $\mathcal O_Z$-algebras.

proof.text: Identify f*i′* with i*g* by uniqueness of left adjoints to the common pushforward. Applying i* to γ_n produces homogeneous comparisons d_n. Their adjoint formulas follow from the adjunction units, and naturality gives the stated affine formula including arbitrary scalar factors. Left adjoints preserve epis; functors preserve isomorphisms.

proof.text: Use the coproduct universal properties and preservation of coproducts by f* to assemble d_n into c. The affine homogeneous representative formulas imply that its module adjoint preserves products and one: apply the affine homogeneous ring-map lemma and check the laws on a compatible affine cover. Its module linearity proves compatibility with structure-sheaf scalars, giving the ring-sheaf adjoint ρ.

source.place: Tags 0634–0635; categorical proof using ideal powers before taking conormal quotients.

proof.text: In degree zero the power comparison is the structure-module comparison; the two composed adjunctions and the commutative square identify its normalization. In degree one the existing canonical conormal map has exactly the same representative formula. Monicity of the ideal-power inclusion and affine sheaf locality give uniqueness of every d_n from that formula. Coproduct uniqueness then gives uniqueness of c.

source.place: Tags 0634–0635; categorical proof using ideal powers before taking conormal quotients.

proof.text: If all d_n are epi, cancellation on each summand and the target coproduct property show c is epi. If g is flat, assemble the inverses of d_n through the target coproduct; both composites are identities by the coproduct hom-extensionality principle. Uniqueness transfers these properties to every base-change map.

(2) The affine-sections lemma on f|_W, and M⊗_{A/J}B/K = M⊗_A B since JM=0. (3) K^n=J^nB and the chart map is well defined.
